clue.text: One way to get rid of the stubble?

definitions.text: One way to get rid of the stubble?

parts.words: One way to get rid of the stubble?
parts.note: a razor run right down to the skin removes stubble, and the same phrase means a narrow escape from danger

explanation.definitionFit: A very near shave of the face is literally the way to clear stubble, and figuratively a narrow escape.

clue.text: Contend successfully in 13 dn.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the letters of the solution to 13 down

parts.note: 13 down is the cross-reference to the solution of that clue

explanation.surface: A competitor holds their own inside some other contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or deal effectively with a difficulty is to contend with it successfully.

clue.text: Henley's musical composition?

parts.note: Henley Regatta is famous for rowing eights, and a piece of music for eight players shares that number

explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames hosts a famous rowing regatta where crews of eight race.
explanation.definitionFit: A group or piece for eight performers matches the crews of eight rowers at Henley.

clue.text: Levy a tax grant ordered in prodigal

definitions.note: an adverb phrase: in prodigal fashion

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of these words are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A demand to raise a tax and make a wasteful grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges LEVYATAXGRANT; 'in prodigal' stands for 'in a prodigal way', an adverb like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending in a prodigal way means spending wastefully and without restraint.

clue.text: Curt report on child who overate at day's party ?

definitions.text: Curt report on child who overate at day's party ?

parts.words: Curt report on child who overate at day's party ?
parts.note: a brief message about a greedy child at a party: sent back to the house feeling ill

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, the phrase is a terse note that a child went back to the house unwell; normally it means longing for one's house.

clue.text: Clearly the place for Brinkmanship.

parts.note: brinkmanship is going to the very edge, so its natural place is the edge or brink

explanation.definitionFit: A border or brink is the edge where brinkmanship pushes matters.

clue.text: Flattering copyists.

parts.note: imitation is said to be the sincerest flattery, and mimicking primates copy others

explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to imitate, the habit for which monkey-like primates are named as imitators.

clue.text: Clay pin adaptable for bending.

definitions.note: used as a noun: the quality of being bendable

indicators.note: adaptable suggests these letters can be shaped into another form

explanation.surface: Clay can be moulded around a pin to bend it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexibility, the capacity for bending, is suppleness.

clue.text: Sulky state? Yes it's the mumps.

definitions.meaning: a sulky state is a moody, resentful silence
the mumps is an old phrase for a fit of sulking

explanation.surface: A child in a bad mood blamed on an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The mumps' here is not the disease: it is a dated term for a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sulky state and a fit of the mumps are moody silent resentment.

clue.text: Small and to the point in embroidery.

definitions.meaning: small in French, used in English phrases such as ... four
... point is a fine needlework stitch, so this word comes before 'point' in embroidery

explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for small and names the fine stitch in needlework called petit point.

clue.text: Unexpected lodger in puma's lair

indicators.note: unexpected signals that the letters turn up in a surprising order

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A surprising guest found in a big cat's den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' rearranges PUMASLAIR; the whole clue also describes the animal, whose young lodge in a pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouched mammal such as a kangaroo carries its young as lodgers, and one turning up in a puma's den would be unexpected.

clue.text: Result of an indifferent tanning

parts.note: too little time in the sun leaves skin pale, as too little light leaves a photograph faint

explanation.definitionFit: Too little exposure to light gives a faint photograph, and too little sun a poor tan.

clue.text: Such superiority passes all limits.

parts.note: a superiority that goes beyond every limit is the very meaning of the word

explanation.definitionFit: Surpassing all limits is the core sense of excelling beyond ordinary bounds.

clue.text: They solve the problem of those who just can't see.

definitions.text: They solve the problem of those who just can't see.

parts.words: They solve the problem of those who just can't see.
parts.note: people who just cannot see over a crowd or above water use a tube of mirrors

explanation.definitionFit: Submarine crews and crowds at parades use mirrored viewing tubes to see over obstacles.

clue.text: "Studious of —— and case"

parts.note: a line from John Gay's Fables, the missing word paired with ease as what a fashionable person studies

explanation.definitionFit: Refined grace of style is what the fashionable lady in the verse studies alongside ease.

clue.text: Chalk white? Could be.

parts.note: a stick of chalky colouring for drawing could well be white

explanation.definitionFit: A drawing stick made of coloured chalk or wax is often white.

clue.text: It suggests there's dissipation in the stronghold.

definitions.text: It suggests there's dissipation in the stronghold.

parts.words: It suggests there's dissipation in the stronghold.
parts.note: fast can mean dissipated, as in fast living, so a word for a fortress sounds like a state of dissipation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means both firm and dissolute; the word for a fortress looks like the quality of loose living.
explanation.definitionFit: A secure, fortified retreat is a stronghold.

clue.text: Where a scene is made just for fun.

definitions.text: Where a scene is made just for fun.

parts.words: Where a scene is made just for fun.
parts.note: a scene belongs inside a drama, and doing something just for fun is doing it jokingly

explanation.definitionFit: A scene sits within a drama, and something said jokingly is said not in earnest.

clue.text: A sorry sort of action.

parts.note: an act done to show one is sorry for wrongdoing

explanation.definitionFit: An act of atonement shows contrition, the feeling of being sorry.

clue.text: That feline type — there's no end

definitions.text: That feline type — there's no end

parts.words: That feline type — there's no end
parts.note: a breed of cat with no tail, the tail being its end

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, gives its name to a tailless cat breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats from the Isle of Man are a breed known for having no tail.

clue.text: Idiot, for example, class one yet has penetration!

parts.note: A1 means first class, written with the letter I for the one

explanation.surface: A fool, though top of the class, still shows real insight.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a rating for the best quality; the figure one is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu throwing spear is a weapon whose purpose is piercing.

clue.text: Party at which the Americans put up their guns?

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: gats is American slang for guns

explanation.surface: A men-only party where Americans display their firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Americans' tells you the guns are the American slang word; 'put up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A party for men only, held for a groom before a wedding.

clue.text: Stalk-and check.

definitions.meaning: to check is to stop a flow

explanation.definitionFit: A plant stalk and stopping a flow, as of blood, share the same word.

clue.text: Not surprising effect of regal pints

definitions.text: Not surprising effect of regal pints

indicators.note: effect of signals the letters are worked on and changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking royal quantities of beer predictably gets you drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect of' rearranges REGALPINTS; the whole clue also says what lots of pints do, plastered being slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being plastered is slang for very drunk, the predictable result of many pints.
